senses.gloss: In a dull way that never changes in tone or pace.
examples: The professor read his notes *monotonously* for an hour.
Rain dripped *monotonously* from the gutter all night.
The days passed *monotonously* on the long voyage.

position: before its word — as an intensifier; end in the manner sense
comparison: more/most — rare; mostly used as an intensifier
modifies: adjectives; verbs in the manner sense

senses.gloss: Extremely — usually about something bad or excessive.
examples: The punishment seemed *monstrously* unfair.
Housing in the city has become *monstrously* expensive.
The project was *monstrously* over budget.

senses.gloss: In a very cruel or wicked way.
examples: The prisoners were treated *monstrously*.
He behaved *monstrously* toward his own family.

senses.gloss: In a gloomy, sulky or bad-tempered way.
examples: The teenager stared *moodily* out the car window.
He sat *moodily* in the corner and refused to talk.
She kicked *moodily* at the snow.

senses.gloss: With an unhealthy interest in death, disease or unpleasant things.
examples: Crowds gathered, *morbidly* curious, around the wreck.
The show is *morbidly* fascinated with serial killers.
He joked *morbidly* about his own funeral.

senses.gloss: To a degree that is dangerous to health — in *morbidly obese*.
examples: The study followed 500 *morbidly* obese adults.
Surgery is usually offered only to patients who are *morbidly* obese.

senses.gloss: In a sullen, unhappy way, without wanting to talk.
examples: He stared *morosely* into his coffee.
"It's going to rain all week," she said *morosely*.
The fans filed *morosely* out of the stadium after the loss.

type: viewpoint — in terms of form or structure
position: before its word — *morphologically similar*; also front

senses.gloss: In terms of the form and structure of living things or of words.
examples: The two species are *morphologically* almost identical.
*Morphologically*, Russian is far more complex than English.
Under the microscope, the cells looked *morphologically* normal.

senses.gloss: In a way that causes death.
examples: The soldier was *mortally* wounded in the attack.
The deer had been *mortally* injured by the car.

senses.gloss: Very seriously or deeply — about feelings.
examples: She was *mortally* offended by his comment.
As a kid I was *mortally* afraid of the dark.

senses.gloss: In a very sad way, as if grieving.
examples: The dog howled *mournfully* at the door.
A train whistle sounded *mournfully* in the distance.
She looked *mournfully* at the empty chair.

senses.gloss: In a way that stirs strong feelings, especially sadness or sympathy.
examples: She spoke *movingly* about her late father.
The book describes the refugees' journey *movingly*.
He wrote *movingly* of his years in the war.

type: manner — involving several countries or groups

senses.gloss: With several countries or parties taking part together.
examples: The president said the problem must be solved *multilaterally*.
The sanctions were agreed *multilaterally* at the summit.
Trade rules work best when they are negotiated *multilaterally*.

type: degree — in more than one way
position: before its word — a participle or adjective (*multiply injured*)
contrast: Spelled exactly like the verb *multiply* (MUHL-tuh-ply, умножать), but the adverb ends in *-plee*. It is formal and appears almost only before a participle or adjective: *multiply injured*, *multiply disabled*, *multiply resistant*.

senses.gloss: In several ways or to several degrees at once.
examples: Paramedics took two *multiply* injured victims to the trauma center.
The school serves *multiply* disabled children from across the county.
Doctors are worried about *multiply* resistant strains of TB.

type: manner — by a city or town government

senses.gloss: By or under the control of a city or town government.
examples: The town gets power from a *municipally* owned utility.
Most of the parks are *municipally* run.
The golf course is *municipally* operated and open to everyone.

senses.gloss: In a way that shows a wish to kill or hurt someone; savagely.
examples: She glared *murderously* at the driver who cut her off.
The two gangs fought *murderously* for control of the block.
He looked at me *murderously* when I told the story.

position: front or end — front as a viewpoint (*Musically, …*); before its word in *musically gifted*

senses.gloss: In terms of music; as far as music is concerned.
examples: *Musically*, the new album is their best work.
Both of her kids are *musically* gifted.
The show looks great, but *musically* it's weak.

senses.gloss: In a thoughtful, slightly dreamy way, as if thinking aloud.
examples: "I wonder what ever happened to her," he said *musingly*.
She gazed *musingly* out at the lake.
He tapped his pen *musingly* against the desk.

senses.gloss: Without speaking.
examples: He nodded *mutely* and left the room.
The kids stared *mutely* at the broken window.
She shook her head *mutely*, too upset to answer.

type: manner — shared by both or all sides

senses.gloss: In a way that is felt, done or shared by each side toward the other.
examples: The deal is *mutually* beneficial for both companies.
We set a *mutually* convenient time for the meeting.
The two plans are *mutually* exclusive — we can only choose one.

position: any position — end or mid for manner; front as a comment (*Mysteriously, …*)

senses.gloss: In a strange way that nobody can explain or understand.
examples: My keys *mysteriously* disappeared from the table.
She smiled *mysteriously* and changed the subject.
*Mysteriously*, the lights came back on by themselves.

senses.gloss: In a spiritual way that goes beyond ordinary understanding.
examples: Many visitors describe the canyon as *mystically* beautiful.
The poet writes *mystically* about nature and God.
The two lovers felt *mystically* connected.

senses.gloss: In a way that shows too little experience and too much trust.
examples: I *naively* believed the landlord would fix the heat.
She trusted him *naively* and lost her savings.
We *naively* assumed the drive would take two hours.

position: before its word — *nakedly ambitious*; also end

senses.gloss: Openly, without any attempt to hide it — usually about something unpleasant.
examples: The ad was a *nakedly* political attack.
He was *nakedly* ambitious from his first day on the job.
Her fear showed *nakedly* on her face.

position: mid — before the verb (*narrowly escaped*); before its word in *narrowly defined*

senses.gloss: Only just; by a very small margin.
examples: The driver *narrowly* avoided hitting a deer.
The bill *narrowly* passed the Senate, 51 to 49.
She *narrowly* missed the bus.

senses.gloss: In a strict or limited way.
examples: The law defines "family" very *narrowly*.
Try not to think about the problem so *narrowly*.

comparison: more/most — in the speech sense only

senses.gloss: With a sound that comes through the nose.
examples: He talks a little *nasally* when he has a cold.
The singer pronounced the vowels *nasally*.

senses.gloss: Through the nose — about taking medicine.
examples: The vaccine is given *nasally* instead of by shot.
This spray should be used *nasally* twice a day.

senses.gloss: In a mean, unkind or unpleasant way.
examples: "Nobody asked you," she said *nastily*.
He laughed *nastily* at my mistake.
The argument ended *nastily*, with both of them yelling.

ru: по всей стране, на национальном уровне
type: place — across a whole country; also viewpoint
position: end; before its word in *nationally televised*

senses.gloss: Across or throughout a whole country; at the level of the country.
senses.ru: по всей стране, на национальном уровне
examples: The game will be *nationally* televised on Sunday.
Locally the store is popular, but *nationally* it's unknown.
The school is ranked 12th *nationally*.

contrast: The same form is an adjective before a noun: *a nationwide search* (общенациональный). As an adverb it follows the verb: *The movie opens nationwide on Friday*, not *opens in nationwide*.

senses.gloss: In every part of a country.
examples: The movie opens *nationwide* on Friday.
The company has 300 stores *nationwide*.
Gas prices rose *nationwide* last month.

position: before its word — almost always *nattily dressed*

senses.gloss: In a neat, stylish way — about clothes.
examples: A *nattily* dressed man held the door for us.
He showed up *nattily* attired in a bow tie.
The band was *nattily* dressed in matching suits.

senses.gloss: In a badly behaved or slightly improper way — often playfully.
examples: The puppy *naughtily* chewed up my slippers.
She grinned *naughtily* and took the last cookie.
The kids in the back row giggled *naughtily* during the speech.

senses.gloss: In a tidy, careful and orderly way.
examples: The towels were *neatly* folded on the bed.
Please write your name *neatly* at the top.
His clothes hung *neatly* in the closet.

senses.gloss: Cleverly and exactly; in a simple, skillful way.
examples: That quote *neatly* sums up the whole book.
She *neatly* avoided answering the question.

position: mid — after *not* or the first auxiliary (*doesn't necessarily mean*)
contrast: Most often negative: *not necessarily* = не обязательно, не всегда. Do not use it for Russian *обязательно* in a request or promise: *Обязательно приходи!* is *Be sure to come!* or *You have to come!*, not *Necessarily come!*; *Я обязательно позвоню* is *I'll definitely call*. On its own, *necessarily* means “as a logical result”, which is formal.

senses.gloss: In every case; for certain — almost always with *not*.
senses.ru: обязательно; *not necessarily* — не обязательно, не всегда
examples: Expensive wine isn't *necessarily* better.
"So you're quitting?" "Not *necessarily*."
A quiet kid doesn't *necessarily* have a problem.

senses.gloss: As a result that cannot be avoided.
examples: A bigger house *necessarily* means higher bills.
The summary is *necessarily* brief.

position: mid; before its word in *needlessly complicated*

senses.gloss: Without any good reason; more than is necessary.
examples: The form is *needlessly* complicated.
Hundreds of people died *needlessly* in the fire.
Don't worry him *needlessly* — wait until we know more.

senses.gloss: In a bad, harmful or disapproving way.
examples: Lack of sleep can *negatively* affect your memory.
Voters reacted *negatively* to the tax plan.
Try not to think so *negatively* about yourself.

senses.gloss: With a negative electric charge.
examples: Electrons are *negatively* charged.
The *negatively* charged ions move toward the positive pole.

senses.gloss: Without the proper care that is expected, often with legal responsibility.
examples: The lawsuit claims the hospital acted *negligently*.
He was accused of driving *negligently* through a school zone.
The landlord *negligently* ignored the broken railing.

senses.gloss: In a worried, anxious or uneasy way.
examples: She laughed *nervously* and looked at the floor.
He waited *nervously* outside the principal's office.
The kids glanced *nervously* at the dark woods.

senses.gloss: In an overly anxious or obsessive way.
examples: He *neurotically* checks the stove five times before leaving.
She is *neurotically* afraid of germs.
I planned every minute of the trip *neurotically*.

position: before its word — a past participle (*newly built*, *newly elected*)
contrast: *newly* goes only before a participle or adjective: *newly married*, *a newly opened store*. It does not modify a finite verb — *He just arrived* or *He arrived recently*, not *He newly arrived*.

senses.gloss: Recently; not long ago.
examples: The *newly* elected mayor gave her first speech.
They're *newly* married and still looking for a house.
We ate at a *newly* opened Thai place downtown.

senses.gloss: Well; in a pleasant or satisfactory way.
examples: Your garden is coming along *nicely*.
The dress fits you *nicely*.
The rice turned out *nicely*.

senses.gloss: Politely or kindly.
examples: If you ask *nicely*, I'll give you a cookie.
Please treat your little brother *nicely*.

senses.gloss: Quickly, lightly and easily in movement or thought.
examples: The goat climbed *nimbly* up the rocks.
Her fingers moved *nimbly* over the keys.
The senator *nimbly* dodged the reporter's question.

senses.gloss: By nine times as much.
examples: Online orders jumped *ninefold* in a single year.
The town's population has grown almost *ninefold* since 1950.
The cost of the project increased *ninefold* from the first estimate.

senses.gloss: In a brave, generous or honorable way.
examples: The firefighters acted *nobly* during the crisis.
He *nobly* offered to take the blame.
She fought *nobly* for the rights of workers.

senses.gloss: At night rather than during the day — mostly about animals.
examples: Most owls hunt *nocturnally*.
In the desert, many animals are active *nocturnally* to avoid the heat.
Raccoons feed *nocturnally* and sleep through the day.

senses.gloss: Without making any sound.
examples: The cat moved *noiselessly* across the rug.
The electric car pulled away *noiselessly*.
He closed the door *noiselessly* behind him.

senses.gloss: With a lot of noise; loudly.
examples: The kids ran *noisily* down the hall.
He slurped his soup *noisily*.
The old refrigerator hums *noisily* all night.

position: before its word — *nominally in charge*; also mid

senses.gloss: In name or on paper, but not in reality.
examples: The king is *nominally* the head of state.
She was *nominally* in charge, but her deputy made the decisions.
The country is *nominally* a democracy.

senses.gloss: Calmly and casually, as if not worried or interested.
examples: He leaned *nonchalantly* against the wall.
"Oh, I won the lottery," she said *nonchalantly*.
The cat walked *nonchalantly* past the barking dog.

contrast: The same form is an adjective: *a nonstop flight* (прямой рейс). As an adverb: *We flew nonstop to Tokyo*.

senses.gloss: Without stopping or pausing.
examples: The baby cried *nonstop* for two hours.
It rained *nonstop* all weekend.
She talks *nonstop* about her new job.

senses.gloss: Without stopping on the way — about a trip.
examples: We flew *nonstop* from Chicago to Rome.
This bus goes *nonstop* to the airport.

senses.gloss: Without words — through gestures, facial expressions or body language.
examples: Babies communicate *nonverbally* long before they talk.
He showed his anger *nonverbally*, by crossing his arms.
Much of what we say, we say *nonverbally*.

senses.gloss: Without using force or violence.
examples: The marchers protested *nonviolently* in front of city hall.
Dr. King urged people to resist *nonviolently*.
The standoff ended *nonviolently*.

contrast: As an adverb it takes no preposition: *drive north*, *head north*, not *drive to north*. Use *to the north* or *in the north* when it is a noun: *They live in the north of the state*. *up north* is common in American speech: *We have a cabin up north*.

senses.gloss: Toward or in the north.
senses.ru: на север, к северу, на севере
examples: We drove *north* along the coast.
Birds fly *north* in the spring.
The town lies about fifty miles *north* of Denver.

form: north + east, written as one word in American English

senses.gloss: Toward or in the northeast.
examples: The storm is moving *northeast*.
The farm is ten miles *northeast* of town.
Head *northeast* until you reach the lake.

form: north + west, written as one word in American English

senses.gloss: Toward or in the northwest.
examples: The trail turns *northwest* after the bridge.
They moved *northwest*, to Seattle.
The airport is about twenty miles *northwest* of the city.

senses.gloss: With a fond, slightly sad longing for the past.
examples: My grandfather talks *nostalgically* about his childhood farm.
She looked back *nostalgically* on her college years.
The movie *nostalgically* recreates small-town life in the 1950s.

type: negative — in no way, not at all
position: before its word — almost only *nothing like*
contrast: Usually *nothing* is a pronoun: *I saw nothing*. The adverb use is fixed: *She looks nothing like her sister* = совсем не похожа. It already carries the negative, so no *not*: *It's nothing like the photo* or *It isn't anything like the photo*, never *It isn't nothing like*.

senses.gloss: Not at all; in no way — in *nothing like*.
examples: She looks *nothing* like her sister.
The hotel was *nothing* like the pictures online.
Honestly, it tastes *nothing* like real chicken.

position: before its word — *noticeably better*; also mid

senses.gloss: In a way that is easy to see or notice.
examples: It's *noticeably* cooler in the mountains.
Her English has improved *noticeably* this year.
He was *noticeably* absent from the party.

position: before its word — *notoriously difficult*; also mid
contrast: *notoriously* is always negative: *notoriously unreliable* = печально известен своей ненадёжностью. For something good use *famously* or *well known for*: *famously generous*, not *notoriously generous*.

senses.gloss: In a way that is widely known — about something bad or difficult.
examples: Parking downtown is *notoriously* difficult.
The weather in Chicago is *notoriously* unpredictable.
That airline is *notoriously* late.

ru: тем не менее, несмотря на это
type: linking — contrast: in spite of what was just said
contrast: Usually a preposition, before or after its noun: *notwithstanding the cost*, *the cost notwithstanding* (несмотря на). Only when it stands alone, with nothing after it, is it the adverb meaning *nevertheless*. Both uses are formal; in speech Americans say *still*, *even so* or *despite that*.

senses.gloss: Nevertheless; in spite of that.
senses.ru: тем не менее, несмотря на это
examples: The reviews were terrible; the movie made millions *notwithstanding*.
The plan has real risks. *Notwithstanding*, the board voted to go ahead.
Many people objected, but the council approved the project *notwithstanding*.

senses.gloss: Without feeling or reacting, as if in shock.
examples: She stared *numbly* at the letter.
He nodded *numbly* as the doctor explained.
We walked *numbly* out of the hospital.

position: end; before its word in *numerically superior*

senses.gloss: In terms of numbers; by number.
senses.ru: численно, по числу; в числовом порядке
examples: The files are sorted *numerically*, not by date.
The enemy was *numerically* stronger but poorly trained.
Express the results *numerically* in a table.

ru: с точки зрения питания, по питательности
position: before its word — *nutritionally balanced*; also front

senses.gloss: In terms of the nutrients food contains.
senses.ru: с точки зрения питания, по питательности
examples: School lunches must be *nutritionally* balanced.
*Nutritionally*, brown rice beats white rice.
Canned beans are *nutritionally* similar to dried ones.

position: after its word — after a number from one to twelve
contrast: Only with whole hours: *at six o'clock*, but *at 6:30* or *at half past six*, never *6:30 o'clock*. Do not add *a.m.* or *p.m.*: say *7 p.m.* or *seven o'clock in the evening*, not *7 o'clock p.m.* Russian *в шесть часов* is *at six o'clock* or just *at six*.

senses.gloss: Used after a number from one to twelve to name an exact hour.
examples: The store opens at nine *o'clock*.
It's almost three *o'clock* — we're going to be late.
I'll meet you at the station at six *o'clock*.

senses.gloss: In a way that does what you are told.
examples: The dog sat *obediently* by the door.
The students *obediently* lined up in the hall.
She *obediently* handed over her phone.

position: any position — end for manner; front as a comment (*Objectively, …*)

senses.gloss: Fairly, based on facts and not on personal feelings.
examples: Try to look at the situation *objectively*.
*Objectively*, it was the better offer.
Judges are supposed to decide cases *objectively*.

senses.gloss: In a willing, helpful way.
examples: The waiter *obligingly* moved us to a quieter table.
A stranger *obligingly* took our picture.
The dog rolled over *obligingly* when the kids asked.

senses.gloss: Indirectly, without saying something openly.
examples: The speech referred only *obliquely* to the scandal.
She hinted *obliquely* that she might leave the company.

senses.gloss: At an angle; not straight.
examples: Late afternoon light fell *obliquely* across the floor.
The road crosses the river *obliquely*.

position: end; before its word in *obnoxiously loud*

senses.gloss: In a very annoying or rude way.
examples: The guy behind us talked *obnoxiously* through the whole movie.
Their music was *obnoxiously* loud.
He bragged *obnoxiously* about his new car.

position: before its word — *obscenely rich*; end in the manner sense
modifies: adjectives; verbs in the manner sense

senses.gloss: Shockingly, unfairly much — about money or excess.
examples: Some CEOs are paid *obscenely* high salaries.
The family is *obscenely* rich.
Tickets were *obscenely* expensive.

senses.gloss: In a sexually offensive or indecent way.
examples: A fan gestured *obscenely* at the referee.
He was fined for swearing *obscenely* on live TV.

position: end; before its word in *obscurely worded*

senses.gloss: In a way that is unclear or hard to understand.
examples: The rule is so *obscurely* worded that nobody follows it.
He hinted *obscurely* at trouble in the family.

senses.gloss: In a vague way that you cannot quite explain — about feelings.
examples: She felt *obscurely* guilty, though she had done nothing wrong.
I was *obscurely* disappointed by the ending.

senses.gloss: Too eager to please or obey, in a way that seems insincere.
examples: The manager smiled *obsequiously* at the rich customer.
He agreed *obsequiously* with everything his boss said.
The staff bowed *obsequiously* as the senator walked in.

senses.gloss: In a way that cannot stop thinking about or doing something.
examples: She checks her email *obsessively*.
He is *obsessively* neat about his desk.
Fans followed the trial *obsessively*.

senses.gloss: Stubbornly, refusing to change your mind.
examples: He *obstinately* refused to see a doctor.
The toddler shook her head *obstinately*.
Prices have stayed *obstinately* high.

position: any position — end for manner; front as a comment (*Oddly enough, …*)

senses.gloss: In a strange or unusual way.
examples: He's been acting *oddly* since the accident.
The house was *oddly* quiet when we got home.
She was dressed *oddly* for a job interview.

senses.gloss: Surprisingly — commenting on a whole statement, often *oddly enough*.
examples: *Oddly* enough, I wasn't nervous at all.
*Oddly*, nobody noticed the missing painting for a week.

position: end; front as a viewpoint in sports (*Offensively, …*)

senses.gloss: In a rude or insulting way.
examples: The comedian was accused of joking *offensively* about immigrants.
He behaved *offensively* toward the waitress.

senses.gloss: In attack — especially in sports, about scoring points.
examples: *Offensively*, the team struggled all season.
They played well *offensively* but gave up too many goals.

form: off + hand, written as one word
contrast: Before a noun it is an adjective meaning careless or casual: *an offhand remark* (небрежное замечание). As an adverb it usually means from memory, right now: *I don't know offhand*.

senses.gloss: Without checking the facts or thinking about it first.
examples: I don't know his phone number *offhand*.
*Offhand*, I'd say it will cost about $500.
Can you remember *offhand* when the meeting starts?

senses.gloss: Casually, as if it were not important.
examples: She mentioned *offhandedly* that she was moving to Texas.
He *offhandedly* dismissed my idea.
"Oh, I got the job," he said *offhandedly*.

contrast: A false friend: *officiously* is not *официально*. That is *officially*. *officiously* is always critical — bossy and too eager to use a little authority.

senses.gloss: In a bossy, self-important way, giving orders or help nobody asked for.
examples: A security guard *officiously* demanded to see our tickets again.
He *officiously* told everyone at the picnic where to park.
The clerk *officiously* pointed out a tiny mistake on my form.

ru: за кулисами, со сцены; в жизни
position: end; front for the private-life sense (*Offstage, …*)
form: off + stage, written as one word

senses.gloss: Off the stage, where the audience cannot see.
senses.ru: за кулисы, за кулисами, со сцены
examples: The actor bowed and walked *offstage*.
We heard a crash *offstage*.

senses.gloss: In a performer's private life.
examples: *Offstage*, the rock star is quiet and shy.
The two comedians were close friends *offstage*.

position: mid — before the main verb; also front (*Oftentimes, …*)
contrast: An American word, common in speech and informal writing; British English treats it as old-fashioned. It means the same as *often* but cannot be compared or modified: *more often*, *very often*, never *more oftentimes*. In formal writing use *often*.

senses.gloss: Often; many times.
examples: *Oftentimes* the simplest answer is the right one.
Kids *oftentimes* understand more than we think.
We'd *oftentimes* stay up talking until two in the morning.

contrast: As an adverb *okay* means acceptably, not especially well: *The interview went okay* = нормально, так себе, not *отлично*. It is informal; in careful writing use *well* or *fine*. Its uses as an adjective (*Are you okay?*) and an interjection (*Okay, let's go*) belong to other word classes.

senses.gloss: Well enough; in an acceptable way.
examples: The interview went *okay*, I guess.
Is the printer working *okay* now?
She's doing *okay* after the surgery.

position: end; mid before an adjective (*ominously quiet*)

senses.gloss: In a way that suggests something bad is going to happen.
examples: Dark clouds gathered *ominously* over the lake.
The engine made an *ominously* loud clunk.
The street was *ominously* quiet.

contrast: The same form is an adjective: *a one-on-one meeting*. British English says *one-to-one*; Americans say *one-on-one*.

senses.gloss: Between two people only, face to face.
senses.ru: один на один, индивидуально, с глазу на глаз
examples: The coach meets *one-on-one* with every player.
I'd like to talk to you *one-on-one* after class.
The tutor works *one-on-one* with struggling readers.

form: on + shore, written as one word
contrast: The opposite of *offshore*. The same form is an adjective: *an onshore wind*, *onshore drilling*.

senses.gloss: Toward the land from the sea, or on land rather than at sea.
senses.ru: на берег, к берегу, на суше
examples: The hurricane is expected to move *onshore* tonight.
The wind was blowing *onshore*, bringing in big waves.
Most of the company's oil is now produced *onshore*.

form: on + stage, written as one word

senses.gloss: On or onto the stage, in front of the audience.
examples: The crowd cheered as the band walked *onstage*.
She's shy in person but fearless *onstage*.
He fell *onstage* during the second act.

senses.gloss: Without hiding anything; publicly and honestly.
examples: We talked *openly* about our money problems.
He was the first *openly* gay member of the city council.
Several players *openly* criticized the coach.

ru: в оперативном отношении, с точки зрения работы
type: viewpoint — in terms of how something runs
position: front or end; before its word in *operationally ready*

senses.gloss: In terms of how an organization, system or machine works day to day.
senses.ru: в оперативном отношении, с точки зрения работы
examples: *Operationally*, the merger went smoothly.
The new plant will be *operationally* ready by June.
The airline is struggling *operationally* and financially.

contrast: Most often a preposition (*the bank opposite the park*) or an adjective (*the opposite side*). It is an adverb only when nothing follows: *She sat down opposite*. For buildings Americans more often say *across the street*: *They live across the street* sounds more natural than *They live opposite*.

senses.gloss: Facing someone or something, on the other side.
examples: I took a seat, and my boss sat down *opposite*.
The man sitting *opposite* kept reading over my shoulder.
There's a school on the corner and a church directly *opposite*.

position: before its word — *oppressively hot*; end in the manner sense
modifies: adjectives; verbs in the manner sense

senses.gloss: Unpleasantly and heavily — about heat, silence or an atmosphere.
examples: It was *oppressively* hot and humid in New Orleans.
The room fell *oppressively* silent.

senses.gloss: Cruelly and unfairly, using power to control people.
examples: The regime ruled *oppressively* for forty years.
Workers said the company was managed *oppressively*.

position: before its word — *optically clear*; end in the manner sense

senses.gloss: In terms of sight or light; by means of light or lenses.
examples: The glass is *optically* clear, so it's used in camera lenses.
The disc is read *optically* by a laser.
Satellite images can be enlarged *optically* without losing detail.

senses.gloss: In the best or most effective way possible.
examples: The software helps the engine run *optimally*.
Plants grow *optimally* at about 75 degrees.
We need to use our budget *optimally*.

position: any position — end for manner; front as a comment (*Optimistically, …*)

senses.gloss: In a hopeful way, expecting things to go well.
examples: She spoke *optimistically* about the company's future.
We *optimistically* packed shorts for the trip.

senses.gloss: In the best case — commenting on an estimate.
senses.ru: при самом лучшем раскладе, в лучшем случае
examples: *Optimistically*, the repairs will take two weeks.
The house will be finished in March, *optimistically*.

senses.gloss: If you choose to; not as a requirement.
examples: The salad can *optionally* be topped with nuts.
Students may *optionally* submit a second essay.
Enter your email address and, *optionally*, a phone number.

position: before its word — *opulently decorated*; also end

senses.gloss: In a rich, expensive and showy way.
examples: The hotel lobby is *opulently* decorated in gold and marble.
They lived *opulently* in a mansion on Lake Michigan.
The guests arrived *opulently* dressed for the gala.

senses.gloss: In speech rather than in writing.
examples: The test will be given *orally*.
These stories were passed down *orally* for generations.
He agreed to the deal *orally* but never signed anything.

senses.gloss: By mouth — about medicine.
examples: Take this medication *orally* with food.
The drug can be given *orally* or by injection.

position: mid — before the main verb; also front (*Ordinarily, …*)

senses.gloss: Usually; in normal circumstances.
examples: *Ordinarily*, I'd say no, but this is an emergency.
The drive *ordinarily* takes about an hour.
He doesn't *ordinarily* drink coffee this late.

senses.gloss: Without artificial chemicals — about farming and food.
examples: All our vegetables are *organically* grown.
The farm raises its chickens *organically*.

senses.gloss: Naturally and gradually, without being forced or planned.
examples: The business grew *organically* from a single food truck.
Their friendship developed *organically* over the years.
